title: Poker Hand Rank
description: Classify a 5-card poker hand into its category. Parse `rank+suit` strings, build a rank histogram, check straight + flush flags, then walk the ranking ladder from royal-flush downward.

notes: Normalize '10' to a single character ('T') so rank ordering uses a simple string index.
The rank ladder must be checked TOP-DOWN: a full-house also matches three-of-a-kind, but we return the stronger category first.
Wheel straight (A-2-3-4-5) is the special case where the ace is low — handle it explicitly because indices wouldn't be consecutive otherwise.

options: The categories are ordered by strength — the first matching category wins, and royal/straight-flush are stronger than four-of-a-kind

questions.q: What is `groups` if the hand is a full house?
Why rewrite '10' to 'T' before indexing into '23456789TJQKA'?
options: So every rank is a single character — index lookup and sorting stay simple

questions.q: How is a flush detected from the parsed `suits` array?

exercises.prompt: Fill in the flush + four-of-a-kind detection.

blanks.hint: compare each suit to the first

L3.prompt: Implement rankHand(cards). Log ranks for: royal flush (TS-AS spades), four kings, full house (KKK + 22), wheel straight (A-5 mixed), pair of nines.
hints: Normalize '10' to a single character first — indexing into a rank string then becomes trivial.
Build a rank histogram and sort counts descending. `[4,1]` = four-of-a-kind, `[3,2]` = full-house, `[2,2,1]` = two-pair.
Check the categories TOP-DOWN: a full house also matches three-of-a-kind, but royal/straight-flush beat everything.
